newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 14.

text.p: PRAVO - Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar reacted to recent news regarding an 11 billion crown debt to the Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka, stating that, "Slovakia has never recognised any debt to any federal organs or the Czech National Bank. It is a debt which does not exist."

- The Czech Republic is best prepared for entry to the EU according to the Commissioner of the European Agricultural Union, Franz Fischler. There is little Czech opposition to the united agricultural policies of the EU, he added.
- According to the vice-chairman of the Czech Communist Party, it is high time for the Czech government to be replaced because the image of the Czech Republic abroad is being tarnished.

- Education Minister Ivan Pilip has promised to investigate the awarding of a contract to the Fortuna publishing company without holding a public tender. The investigation will look into whether or not the contract was awarded on the basis of illegal contacts between any Education Ministry employees and Fortuna as well as the profitability of the contract.

- Approximately 93,000 students offered 220,000 applications for post-secondary school studies. Economics was the most popular area of study with 22 percent of the applications, followed by education with 20 percent.
- Ceskomoravska Hypotecni Banka lowered its interest rate on mortgage loans from 13.5 percent per annum to 11.9 percent with state support of 7.9 percent.

- Vychodoslovenske Zelezarny Kosice (VSZ) currently controls a fifth of Trinecke Zelezarny (TZ) according to a spokeswoman for TZ, Bohdana Horackova. VSZ purchased a block of shares on the RM-System at the end of last week.

- Minister of Industry and Trade, Vladimir Dlouhy signed a free trade agreement with the Lithuanian Economic Minister Antanas Zenonas Kaminskas, effective January 1, 1997. Lithuania is the Czech Republic's largest trading partner in the Baltics.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - A strong flow of money from smaller banks to larger banks has continued this year as clients indicate their lack of trust in the smaller monetary institutions.
- The Czech Statistics Office published new estimates for macroeconomic growth with slightly lower inflation and higher industrial growth.
